Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per discussion, Atlas is asking to reassign 250 GPU-hours/month currently scoped under Exhibit B into Exhibit C (specialized inference pool) and to apply the tiered pricing that sits on Exhibit C rather than the standard Exhibit B rates. The high-level asks:

- Move 250 GPU-hours/month from Exhibit B to Exhibit C effective 2026-11-01.
- Apply Exhibit C tiered unit pricing (see attached spreadsheet).
- Short SOW edit to call out the carve-out and a 90-day implementation window for routing and prefix cache tuning.

I've attached a single-page summary (Atlas_Requested_Change_Summary.pdf) with our proposed cadence and internal approvals. Carl (copied) will handle legal review on our side; please advise what version you will provide and an estimated turnaround for redlines and a signed addendum.

Appreciate a quick confirmation of next steps.

Thanks,

Atlas Health

Maya — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. We're able to support the reassignment but need to align on three things before we produce a formal addendum:

1) Pricing floor: Exhibit C's tier breaks will apply, but the master fee schedule requires a minimum monthly commitment for Exhibit-level reassignments. Are you comfortable keeping the same minimum commitment (50k nominal) or do you want to propose a pro-rated minimum?

2) Implementation acceptance criteria: we'll include a short SOW exhibit that lists routing rules, cache warm-up plan, and a one-week acceptance test. Please confirm any regulatory audit windows that need to be considered (HIPAA audit window for Atlas).

3) Signatory path: do you want Atlas legal to sign the addendum in DocuSign or will procurement route to your Executive Procurement signatory?

I'll loop in Jonas and Laura to draft redlines. Expect a first-pass redline doc by Wednesday (2026-09-29). If that timing needs to be faster, let me know and we'll prioritize.

Attachments: none on our side for this message.

Best,

Soojin / Laura — attached is our first-pass redline of the order form and a focused exhibit (Redwood_ExhibitB_to_C_redline.docx). Key legal points we adjusted:

- Explicit effective date clause: "effective on the first day of the calendar month following execution" to avoid partial-month billing disputes.
- Minimum commitment handling: If Atlas reduces committed capacity on Exhibit B, they must either (a) reallocate another Exhibit or (b) trigger a 30-day true-up at Exhibit B rates for the prior billing period. We included a pro-rata option for the first 3 months to make the transition smoother.
- Audit & data retention: added a short paragraph pointing to the existing DPA and a one-time operational evidence exchange window (10 business days) for audit artifacts.
- Implementation SLA: added 7 business day cutover window and a one-week acceptance test; failure of acceptance triggers a rollback process with cost reconciliation.

I tried to keep commercial language minimal so the doc reads cleanly for procurement. If we want to be more flexible on the minimum commitment clause I can propose alternative language that allows a temporary reduction tied to a quarterly review.

Attachments: Redwood_ExhibitB_to_C_redline.docx
